model: Regulated utility FCFE at cost of equity (rate-base reinvestment, engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: eps_3yr_cagr (FY2022 $4.68 -> FY2025 $5.66), corroborated by management's 6-7% adjusted-EPS CAGR guidance for 2026-2030
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 4.9% diverges >30% from EPS 5-yr CAGR 11.5%; the EPS figure is distorted by the COVID-depressed FY2020 base ($3.29) and FY2023 ($7.25) carries the Clean Energy Businesses sale gain. Book equity grows through issuance (14.5m shares in FY2025) as well as retention, so equity CAGR overstates per-share compounding. The 3-yr EPS CAGR of 6.5% is the cleanest series and matches guidance.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: the owner-FCFE series (dividends less equity issuance) is positive in FY2022 (~+$1.1B, no issuance) and negative in FY2025 (-$205m), so a compound rate is undefined. Reported OCF-less-capex has been negative every year since FY2016 (capex supercycle); it is not a growth series. Revenue CAGRs include pass-through commodity cost swings (FY2025 +10%) and are not a rate-base growth measure; rate base is guided at ~8%/yr.

scenario_narratives.base: Con Edison executes the approved 2026-2028 multi-year rate plans and the ~$38B 2026-2030 capital plan, growing rate base ~8%/yr and net income ~9%/yr; ~$1.4-1.85B/yr of equity issuance dilutes that to a 5.5-6% EPS CAGR, the low end of the 6-7% guide. Dividends grow ~3%/yr, so through 2030 the cash returned to shareholders roughly equals the cash raised from them -- value is almost entirely the post-2030 phase when growth slows toward 3.5% and 60% of earnings become distributable. The axes are earned ROE versus the 9.25% authorised, the pace of NYPSC-approved rate-base growth, and the cost of the equity needed to fund it; discounted at a 7.25% cost of equity with a terminal multiple of ~16x earnings.
scenario_narratives.bull: Earned ROE closes the gap to authorised as regulatory lag falls under the multi-year plans, electrification load (44% of new-business requests) and the CET transmission JVs add rate base beyond the plan, and net income compounds ~10.5%/yr to 2030 (EPS ~7%, top of guide). The payout is held at ~55% so dividends grow 4.5%/yr. Terminal growth of 4% reflects a multi-decade electrification capex runway in the densest service territory in the US. The terminal value hits the 30x-FCFE cap (~16.7x terminal earnings), so the bull case does not assume a re-rating above sector multiples.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 rate case -- where the NYPSC cut the original electric revenue request by ~87% in year one -- is the template rather than the exception: affordability politics in NYC compress earned ROE to ~8.25%, parts of the plan are disallowed or deferred, rate-base growth slows to ~6% and net income to 6%/yr, leaving EPS roughly flat after dilution. Management trims issuance with the plan, so near-term FCFE is slightly better than base, but the terminal earnings base is 19% smaller and terminal growth 3%. Steam (5% of revenue) decays under Local Law 97 electrification. No solvency element: the bear is a regulated-return squeeze, not a balance-sheet event.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated utility is a claim on rate base x allowed ROE, funded by a mix of retained earnings and new equity; the cash that actually reaches existing shareholders is dividends less the equity they are asked to put back in. This model values that free cash flow to equity directly at a 7.25% cost of equity, with net debt held at zero because the flows are already after interest. Through 2030 the FCFE is roughly nil -- every dollar of dividend is matched by a dollar of issuance -- so the value sits in the post-2030 slowdown when the payout becomes real; that makes the answer a function of terminal growth, cost of equity and the assumed terminal reinvestment rate far more than of any near-year. At the 2026-09-25 close the stock trades close to the probability-weighted value: the market is pricing roughly the base case at a ~7.2% cost of equity, i.e. a bond-proxy return of ~3.3% dividend yield plus ~3-4% growth. A 15% hurdle cannot be met at anything near today's price, which is the normal result for a slow-growing, terminal-heavy asset and not a defect.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: +/-50bp moves the base value by roughly +/-10%; a higher-for-longer rate environment compresses the bond-proxy multiple directly
Terminal reinvestment rate and growth: the post-2030 payout assumption (60% of NI distributable at 3.5% growth) is where nearly all the value sits and is the least observable input
NYPSC regulatory/political risk on authorised ROE and cost recovery (2026 rate case cut ~87% of the year-one electric ask)
Equity issuance price: ~$6B of issuance 2026-2029 at a lower share price raises the dilution cost of the same rate-base growth

Book effective tax rate used as the cash rate by design; if Con Edison were allowed to retain cash-tax benefits the model is conservative, if the rate rises toward 25% (Q1 2026 ran 24.7%) NI is ~2.5% lower
Steam segment stranded-asset risk under Local Law 97 and the CLCPA gas-transition mandate
FY0 balance-sheet anchors are the 2025-12-31 10-K (debt) and 2026-03-31 10-Q (equity, cash); the June 2026 10-Q was not yet in the XBRL API

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 94.96-116.23
data_sources.financials: ED_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (SEC XBRL, FY2009-FY2025 and Q1 2026) plus SEC companyfacts API for FY2025 pre-tax income, income tax, interest expense, dividends paid, equity issuance and the diluted share count
data_sources.qualitative: ED_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): Q2 2026 results, FY2026 guidance ($6.00-6.20 adj EPS, 6-7% EPS CAGR 2026-30, ~$38B 2026-30 capital plan, ~8% rate-base growth, $1.85B 2026 / $4.3B 2027-29 equity), 2026-28 NYPSC rate plan outcome

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement share-based compensation add-back (core_metrics stock_based_comp, $55m); ED publishes no combined equity-award-tax figure and net-share-settlement withholding is immaterial for a utility, so the add-back is used as is
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 for debt (FY2025 10-K); equity and cash refreshed to 2026-03-31 (Q1 2026 10-Q). The Q2 2026 10-Q (June 2026 balance sheet) is not yet in the SEC XBRL companyfacts API as of the valuation date.
inputs.share_count_basis: 361.1m common shares outstanding at 2025-12-31 (FY2025 10-K; diluted weighted average for FY2025 was 358.7m). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed inside net income, and the genuine non-SBC issuance (the $1.85B 2026 and $4.3B 2027-29 equity programme) is deducted from the flows as part of the equity reinvestment line, so the count must not be grown as well. The count is deliberately the 2025-12-31 figure rather than the 368.5m cover-page count at 2026-04-30, because the latter already includes the $776m February 2026 issue that Y1 (FY2026) flows deduct in full; using both would charge the same $776m twice (~$2/share).
inputs.debt_memo: Actual balance sheet: total debt $26,051m and cash $1,629m at 2025-12-31 (net debt $24,422m); cash $147m at 2026-03-31; operating lease liability $500m. Net debt is set to ZERO in the engine because the flows are FREE CASH FLOW TO EQUITY (after the $1,233m FY2025 interest expense) discounted at the cost of equity; subtracting debt again would deduct it twice.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flows are post-interest. USD build: 10-year US Treasury ~4.15% (Sep 2026), equity beta 0.55 (five-year monthly, bond-proxy utility), ERP 5.5% -> CAPM 7.2%; rounded to 7.25% and applied identically to all three scenarios so that regulatory and execution risk is charged once, in the flows. For reference: authorised ROE ~9.25% is a regulatory book return, not a market discount rate; ED's senior unsecured debt costs ~5.3%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases ($500m liability at 2025-12-31) left as an operating cost inside pre-tax income; lease liabilities excluded from the (zero) net-debt bridge. One treatment, consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests; net income is fully attributable to common shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Regulated utility FCFE (free cash flow to equity) capitalised at the cost of equity, run through the owner-FCF component engine. Rationale: the SKILL.md routing table has no regulated-utility row; ED's reported FCF (OCF less capex) is structurally negative for the whole 2026-2030 $38B capital plan (capex ~$7.3B rising to ~$9.1B against D&A of $2.3B) and an unlevered DCF would be >100% terminal value against $24B of net debt on a $37B market capitalisation. A rate-regulated business is priced on rate-base growth x allowed ROE; the folder's precedent for that is the FCFE-at-cost-of-equity engine route (NAB.AX, IAG.AX: net_debt = 0, flows already post-interest). ENGINE MAPPING (read the sliders with this key): 'revenue' = total operating revenues; 'EBITDA margin' = (pre-tax income + D&A + SBC) / revenue, i.e. EBITDA AFTER interest expense and other income, NOT operating EBITDA (FY2025 operating EBITDA margin was 30.8%; the engine's FY2025-equivalent is 29.2% = (2,597 + 2,321 + 55) / 17,049); 'D&A' = book depreciation and amortisation (FY2025 $2,321m, 13.6% of revenue, rising toward 17% as rate base outgrows revenue); 'cash tax rate' = the BOOK effective tax rate (FY2025 22.1%, Q1 2026 24.7%; 23% used) because under cost-of-service ratemaking the cash-tax savings from bonus depreciation reduce rate base and accrue to customers, not shareholders -- ED's cash taxes were a $165m refund in FY2025 and that benefit is deliberately not projected; so engine EBIT = pre-tax income and NOPAT = GAAP net income; 'capex' = D&A + the equity reinvestment required to fund rate-base growth (book-equity growth = NI - dividends + equity issuance for 2026-2030 per the funding plan, then NI x g/ROE for 2031-2035), so that owner FCF = NI - equity reinvestment = FREE CASH FLOW TO EQUITY = dividends - equity issuance. Working capital 0. FY0 = FY2025 (revenue 17,049; NI 2,023; dividends paid 1,166; equity issued ~1,371 (14.5m new shares); FCFE -205). last_fcf = -205 is FY2025 FCFE with SBC charged; reported_fcf = -150 is the same flow with SBC added back (it is NOT OCF less capex, which was about -$1.1B and is not the flow this model values). Y1 = FY2026 (adj EPS guidance $6.00-6.20 on ~367m weighted shares -> NI ~$2.24B base) and is discounted one full period per house convention, which is slightly conservative nine months into the year. TERMINAL CAP: terminal_cap_multiple is 30x terminal FCFE, which at a terminal reinvestment rate of ~40% of NI equals ~16-17x terminal earnings, the regulated-utility sector's long-run median P/E; the tech default of 20x FCFE would be ~11x P/E and would bind in every scenario. Buybacks: none (Con Edison is a net ISSUER; buyback_cash 0). Price is the 2026-09-25 regular close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: Underlying schedule ($m): NI 2,200 (bottom of FY2026 guidance) growing only 6%/yr 2027-2030 (affordability politics after the 2026 rate case -- where ~87% of the year-one electric ask was cut -- compress earned ROE toward 8.25%, disallow part of the plan and slow rate-base growth to ~6%; EPS roughly flat-to-2% after dilution), then 5/4.5/4/3.5/3% 2031-35. DPS grows 2%/yr; issuance cut to 1,200/yr 2027-29 and 1,100 in 2030 as the capex plan is trimmed -- which is why near-term FCFE is HIGHER than base; the damage is a 19% smaller terminal earnings base. Reinvestment 2031-35 = 55/48/42/36/36% of NI at 8.25% ROE. FCFE: -600, 120, 180, 250, 410, 1,312, 1,585, 1,838, 2,099, 2,162. Terminal g 3.0%.

base.narrative: Underlying schedule ($m): NI 2,240 (FY2026, guidance midpoint) growing 9%/yr 2027-2030 (8% rate-base growth plus modest earned-ROE recovery under the 2026-28 multi-year rate plan; implies ~5.8% EPS CAGR after ~3.5%/yr dilution, the low end of the 6-7% guide), then 7.5/6.5/5.5/4.5/4.0% 2031-35 as the capital plan matures. Dividends: DPS $3.40 growing 3%/yr x rising share count (1,250 -> 1,610 by 2030). Equity issuance: 1,850 (2026), 1,430/yr 2027-29, 1,400 (2030) per the funding plan. Equity reinvestment 2031-35 = 78/65/54/46/40% of NI (glide from the plan-year ~93% toward g/ROE at 9% ROE). FCFE: -600, -100, 0, 90, 210, 748, 1,267, 1,757, 2,155, 2,490. Terminal g 3.5% (electrification-driven rate-base growth at inflation-plus).

bull.narrative: Underlying schedule ($m): NI 2,270 (top of FY2026 guidance) growing 10.5%/yr 2027-2030 (rate base 8-9% with earned ROE reaching the ~9.25% authorised level and CET transmission JV income scaling; ~7% EPS CAGR, top of guide), then 8.5/7.5/6.5/5.5/4.5% 2031-35. DPS grows 4.5%/yr (payout held ~55%); same issuance plan as base. Reinvestment 2031-35 = 79/68/58/47/42% of NI at 9.5% ROE. FCFE: -600, -80, 40, 160, 310, 771, 1,263, 1,766, 2,351, 2,688. Terminal g 4.0%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 30x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because Con Edison is a single-regulator dependency (NYPSC sets essentially all of its earnings) and the 2026 rate case demonstrated live political pressure on returns in an affordability-sensitive territory. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right -- earned ROE reaching authorised, full execution of a $38B plan on budget, and equity markets absorbing ~$6B of issuance without a wider discount -- and the terminal value is already capped at sector multiples. Base 50%: the multi-year rate plans through 2028 give unusually good visibility on the central path.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
